title: Future Guelph progress report and local boards
subtitle: Delegations on conservation lands, the Emma Earl bridge and Allen's dam; reports from the Elliott, GRCA, library, police and public health.
overview: A special Council meeting reviewed the first full year of reporting under the Future Guelph strategic plan. Staff said the city now reports on all of its key performance indicators, up from 58% the year before. Results were mixed: housing, transit and downtown renewal showed progress, while environment targets were the weakest area. Council received the progress report {{vote:m1}}. Staff also launched a new public progress website.

Delegates raised three issues. Two asked Council to press the Grand River Conservation Authority (GRCA) over the Hanlon Creek lands in its Nisca management plan, which it has approved for possible sale. Others criticized the Emma Earl bridge project, and one group urged study of removing Allen's dam. Staff said a report on the conservation lands would come to Council after the GRCA board decides, and a report on the downtown bridge and dam environmental assessment is expected in October.

Council then heard from the Elliott Community, the GRCA, the public library, Guelph Police Services and Wellington-Dufferin-Guelph Public Health. Police reported lower overtime and new units on intimate partner violence and human trafficking. Public health warned that funding growth is expected to trail rising costs. One by-law was approved {{vote:m2}}.

decisions.detail: Council received the first full-year report on the Future Guelph strategic plan, covering 2024 results for city services and local boards {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Two delegates argued the Hanlon Creek lands were bought largely with city tax dollars and provincial money. They said the GRCA's plan to declare part of them surplus risks leaving the city with no land and no proceeds. They asked that the plan come to Council.

Staff replied that the matter is not off the radar and has been discussed with the GRCA for a couple of years. They said a decision from the GRCA board is needed first, and that legal staff are looking into the original acquisition conditions. Several councillors asked that the eventual report be public where possible.

A delegate for residents near the Emma Earl bridge criticized the consultation, communications, cost and environmental effects, and called for an independent inquiry. A councillor noted a newsletter with construction updates had been sent in May. Staff rejected the allegations and said the project followed its environmental assessment.

A delegate group urged Council to ask the GRCA to model removing Allen's dam, citing flood risk. The GRCA's CAO said its hydrology work could be coordinated with staff but did not commit to including the dam. The GRCA also said only about 1% of its land met the threshold for disposal.

A councillor asked about overtime across emergency services. Staff said overtime is needed to maintain minimum service levels, and a report on provincial presumptive WSIB legislation is due in September.
